## Microsoft Ignite 2026: Building Windows for the next era of work

• Pavan Davuluri, Executive Vice President, Windows + Devices

Every major shift in computing has changed what people can do at work, and Windows has been at the center. Today, it runs critical work inside your organizations , on over a billion devices across the world . That is a privilege and a responsibility . I t’s why, above all else , we’re moving faster than ever on security so you can build on a foundation of trust and lead in the era of Hybrid Intelligence .

Agents are the next shift in computing . Over the past year, organizations have moved AI from pilots into daily work, and agents are now taking on tasks across apps, files , and systems. In conversations with technology leaders, the questions they’re asking have evolved . They are past debating whether to adopt AI . They are turning to agents and want to know how to run them securely, and how to scale outcomes without cost or risk growing faster than value.

Today at Ignite, we announced:

• A trusted, secure, and more resilient foundation. The Windows endpoint security platform and Windows administrator protection are now generally available, Windows baseline protection is in preview, and Windows Autopatch customers deploy updates over 40% faster than with on-premises management.

• The most secure platform for agents. New containment capabilities in Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), which OpenAI and Meta are already building on, and Windows 365 for Agents, now eligible for Copilot Credits.

• Hybrid Intelligence at work. GitHub Copilot Fusion can now route coding work to local models on developer PCs, in preview, and local context, actions and models are coming soon to Copilot on Copilot+ PCs.

• One estate, from the PC to Azure built as connected AI infrastructure. Direct Stream for Windows 365, and Windows Server 2028 in public preview, with Microsoft Foundry and support for new AI hardware from AMD and NVIDIA.

## A trusted, secure, and more resilient foundation

Critical work happens on Windows, and staying protected while threats evolve has never been more important. That starts with a trusted, secure, and more resilient Windows foundation. We are making investments to harden the platform, make it easier to protect and manage devices, and keep them current.

Historically, some security protections ran in the Windows kernel, where one failure could affect the entire device. In 2024, we started working with our security partners on a more resilient approach. Today, the Windows endpoint security platform is generally available . It lets security providers move critical protections from kernel mode to user mode, making Windows more resilient while preserving the protection customers expect. We are deeply grateful to the ecosystem partners who have built on the platform with us, including Bitdefender, CrowdStrike, ESET, SentinelOne, Sophos, Trellix and TrendAI.

We’re also making device security easier to verify. Windows baseline protection, now in preview in the Windows Insider Program, brings foundational protections like secure boot, virtualization-based security and memory integrity together into one verifiable security state. People get better visibility into the security posture of their PC, and IT gets a clear yes-or-no answer for every device in the fleet. Application developers can use baseline protection to verify that the devices running their applications meet their security requirements. The baseline will continue to evolve as we raise the bar in security.

We are proud to be collaborating with partners from across the ecosystem to see how Windows baseline protection helps meet their needs.

We’re also making it easier to protect your devices from the risks that come with elevated privilege. With Windows administrator protection, now generally available, IT can enable local administrators to run with standard user privileges by default. When a task needs administrator rights, Windows Hello verifies the user and grants those rights to that task alone. When the task ends, so do the elevated privileges, and the risk that came with them.

The same AI that’s helping organizations scale is also helping attackers move faster. Our latest Microsoft Digital Defense Report found that weaponizing a vulnerability, which once took expert skills, now takes just one prompt. New vulnerabilities across the industry are on track to double this year. We’re using AI to stay ahead. MDASH , Microsoft Security’s multi-model agentic scanning harness, now scans Windows code at a scale we’ve never had before, finding vulnerabilities earlier and fixing them faster. In October alone, we shipped fixes for more than 1,100 vulnerabilities, more than in all of 2025. Those fixes only protect your employees once they reach your devices.

Our fastest customers deploy security updates to more than two-thirds of their devices within a week. Windows Autopatch helps more organizations move at that speed: on average, Autopatch customers deploy updates over 40% faster than customers using on-premises management, and usage has grown more than 50% in the last year, to over 150 million enrolled devices. Autopatch now also gives IT more control over updates, better visibility into the features they include and fewer interruptions, with one reboot a month.

The same management principles now apply to apps. With Microsoft Intune Enterprise App Management, IT can deploy and manage apps at scale and can now preview automatic updates not just for the applications they deploy, but the applications people install themselves, with the same controls and deadlines they know from Windows Autopatch.

Windows is also standardizing on declarative management, so devices keep themselves in the state IT defines. Policies such as Wi-Fi and VPN apply, within minutes and stay protected from drift, even when a device is offline.

أعلنت مايكروسوفت خلال مؤتمر Ignite 2026 حزمة جديدة لجعل Windows أساساً آمناً وموثوقاً في عصر وكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي، الذين باتوا ينفذون مهام عبر التطبيقات والملفات والأنظمة.

• منصة أمان نقاط النهاية في Windows وحماية المسؤول في Windows أصبحتا متاحتين عموماً، وحماية خط الأساس في Windows بنسخة تجريبية.
• عملاء Windows Autopatch ينشرون التحديثات أسرع بأكثر من 40% مقارنة بالإدارة المحلية.
• قدرات احتواء جديدة في Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) تبني عليها OpenAI وMeta، وWindows 365 for Agents أصبح مؤهلاً لرصيد Copilot Credits.
• يمكن لـ GitHub Copilot Fusion توجيه مهام البرمجة إلى نماذج محلية على أجهزة المطورين (نسخة تجريبية)، وسيصل السياق والإجراءات والنماذج المحلية قريباً إلى Copilot على أجهزة Copilot+ PC.
• Windows Server 2028 في معاينة عامة مع Microsoft Foundry ودعم عتاد جديد من AMD وNVIDIA.

تبرز أهمية الإعلان في أنه يعالج سؤال المؤسسات الأهم: كيف تشغّل الوكلاء بأمان وتوسّع النتائج دون أن ترتفع التكلفة والمخاطر أسرع من القيمة.
